spatial_claims.claim: D lies between A and G on a line segment, so AD + DG = AG
E is the midpoint of segment DG (DE = EG = (1/2)DG), so E lies between D and G
H lies between A and G on segment AG, with AH + HG = AG and AH * HG = (1/4) sq(DG)

D lies between A and G, creating the third apotome AD and annex DG. E is the midpoint of DG, lying between D and G. H lies between A and G, determined by the rectangle application of 10.17. The auxiliary lines o and p are defined purely by area equations (sq(o) = r * AH, sq(p) = r * HG) and have no specified spatial positions. Steps 4-16 are entirely algebraic, dealing with commensurability, mediality, ratios, and classification of irrational lines. No angles, triangles, circles, or complex spatial configurations appear anywhere in the proof.
